findings.text: The comoving-observer restriction appears nowhere in the statement text. The certificate confines the result to 'comoving lines; all normals only to constant-cosmic-time FLRW slices' (scope.geodesic_coverage) and keeps 'general FLRW, tilted observers or all normals of arbitrary Cauchy surfaces' in not_established; FORMULATION.md's boundary section says 'It does not cover tilted observers, normals to other slices'. The pinned A.2 statement's tail kept 'general-background/geodesic coverage' open, but this statement's tail says only 'general-background coverage', silently dropping the geodesic/observer qualifier, while the clause 'For every Hadamard target state, A.2 becomes an absolute bound' reads as observer-unqualified. Since the receipt binds to the statement text, the comoving-sampling scope is a hidden hypothesis of the stated bound. [Statement clauses 'For every Hadamard target state, A.2 becomes an absolute bound...' and '...general-background coverage and full P8(a) remain open' vs radiation-reference.json scope.geodesic_coverage and not_established ('general FLRW, tilted observers or all normals of arbitrary Cauchy surfaces'); FORMULATION.md 'Boundary of the result'; A.2 dependency tail 'general-background/geodesic coverage']

The counting PASS replay's binary_hash equals the current v1 stamp, so the committed certificate is reproduced by the certified checker for these exact formulas at the exact statement text.
